headings.text: Myth: creatine is only for men
Myth: creatine is only for the gym
Myth: creatine gummies are just candy

myth-pdp.text:
Clinical facts  over
common myths.
TRY Arq8™ NOW
Myth: creatine is only for men

Women naturally produce 20–40% less creatine than men — and levels fluctuate further during menstrual cycles, perimenopause, and menopause. Creatine supports lean muscle, cognitive clarity, mood stability, and bone density. Women don't just benefit from creatine — they may need it more.

Myth: creatine is only for the gym

Your brain consumes creatine too. It supports mental energy, focus under stress, and resilience on low-sleep days.

Myth: creatine = bulky look

Creatine doesn't make you bulky. It supports strength, tone, and recovery by helping your muscles recycle energy faster. How you look depends on how you train and eat. Creatine just makes your effort go further.

Myth: creatine makes you bloated

Old-generation creatine doesn't dissolve fully — large particles sit outside the cell, pull water, and cause that puffy, bloated feeling. FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine is engineered for complete solubility. It absorbs efficiently, gets into the cell, and doesn't cause water retention, bloating or GI discomfort.

Myth: creatine damages your kidneys

It has been clinically proven that creatine does not damage kidneys. In healthy individuals, 5g daily of creatine monohydrate shows no adverse effects on kidney function — even in long-term use. This myth comes from confusing creatine with creatinine, a waste marker. They're not the same thing.

Myth: creatine gummies are just candy

Most are. Many contain less creatine than claimed, use cheap forms that don't absorb well, and coat with sugar. Every batch of Arq8 is third-party tested and provides a verified 5g clinical dose of FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine — plus Taurine, Succinic Acid, and Zinc. This isn't candy. It's a scientifically formulated functional gummy.

headings.text: Is creatine safe for daily use?
When will I start seeing results?
Does creatine have any side effects?

faq.text:
Questions?
We've got answers.
Is creatine safe for daily use?

Yes. Creatine is one of the most studied supplements in existence — with over 700 clinical studies and 30+ years of research confirming its safety for long-term daily use in healthy adults. No cycling required.

When should I take creatine?

Any time. Creatine doesn't work like a stimulant — it works by maintaining consistent levels in your muscle and brain tissue around the clock. Morning, evening, with food or without. The only thing that matters is taking it every day.

Will this cause bloating?

Not with Arq8™. Bloating from creatine is caused by undissolved particles sitting in the gut. FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine dissolves completely — which means nothing sits unabsorbed, and your digestive system never has to deal with the residue that causes discomfort.

Is creatine only for athletes?

No. Your brain uses creatine just as much as your muscles do. Creatine supports mental clarity, focus, stress resilience, and cognitive performance under fatigue — making it as relevant for professionals, parents, and anyone under daily demand as it is for athletes.

When will I start seeing results?

Most people notice subtle improvements in energy and focus within the first one to two weeks. Full muscle and brain saturation typically occurs around 30 days of consistent daily use — which is when the deeper benefits become most noticeable.

Does creatine have any side effects?

Creatine is exceptionally well tolerated. The side effects most people associate with it — bloating, cramping, digestive discomfort — are caused by poor solubility in standard forms, not by creatine itself. FullDissolve™ eliminates those issues. No stimulants. No hormones. Nothing artificial.
